hypothesis.title: The Task-Relevant Signal
hypothesis.question: What should a musical system preserve when full fidelity is impossible or unnecessary?
hypothesis.hypothesis: Musical detail should be allocated toward the task that must survive: function, identity, process evidence, coherent relation, or performer fingerprint. A passage that preserves task-relevant structure under degradation is compositionally stronger than one that merely preserves more surface detail.
hypothesis.rationaleMd: ClariCodec separates intelligibility from acoustic reconstruction detail by optimizing 200 bps speech with WER-driven reinforcement learning [S5]. The Nyishi/Adi analysis shows that low-frequency amplitude modulation carries language identity before MFCC spectral detail is added [S3]. WST-X preserves deformation-stable, multi-scale evidence of synthetic speech rather than reconstructing the whole signal [S6]. The HHL melody-harmony architecture makes the same point abstractly: relation must sometimes remain coherent until measurement, because exposing the intermediate output can destroy the advantage [S1]. Basso continuo griffs show that human style also has local extractable features [S2].

recipe.title: Representation Budget Etudes
recipe.bodyMd: Write four 45-second etudes from the same eight-bar harmonic skeleton. In the intelligibility version, strip the material until root motion, cadence, and phrase rhythm remain [S5]. In the identity version, preserve macro-rhythm and envelope motion while varying pitch and timbre [S3]. In the artifact version, add one subtle synthetic trace and test whether the process remains detectable [S6]. In the coherence version, compose melody and harmony only as coupled pairs, delaying commitment until both layers imply each other [S1]. Render mono, low-bitrate, and lead-muted degradations, then score whether function, identity, and process survive.

parameters.value: 1-5 survival score for function, identity, and process
mono downmix, low-bitrate export, lead-muted render

dawChecklist: Create one eight-bar harmonic skeleton and duplicate it into four 45-second sessions.
Version 1: reduce the arrangement to functional harmonic and rhythmic cues.
Version 2: keep macro-envelope rhythm stable while changing pitch and timbre.
Version 3: add one detectable synthetic process trace without making it foreground material.
Version 4: write melody and harmony as coupled two-event units before committing either layer.
Export full, mono, low-bitrate, and lead-muted versions.
Score function, identity, and process survival from 1 to 5 for each export.

protocol.listeningContext: studio monitors or neutral headphones, level matched
protocol.listeningMethod: blind-ish shuffle among degradation renders; score survival before comparing full mixes
